caption: (a) Panorama 7y3sRwLe3Va-19 and (b) room context. (c) A29 bridges the fireplace with 4 corners; (d) A59 traces its sides with 8. The footprints share a scale, with the reference dashed; the lower row shows the room context and the 3D layouts reconstructed from each annotation.

Overview of the study. Independent Manual and Semi submissions provide spatial observations; geometric quality measurement and structural consensus support controlled comparisons of individuals, group size, team composition and cross-view patterns.

Image observations and reconstructed geometry. A floor endpoint displacement from P to P' changes the footprint and the corresponding wall in 3 dimensions. The assessed layout is blue and the reference is dashed gray.

Controlled endpoint edits and their geometric effects. Both rows start from the same $4\times4$ m room with 3 m walls and a 1.6 m camera height. 1 endpoint moves upward by 24 pixels in a $1024\times512$ panorama while its partner stays fixed. Each row shows the image edit, footprint, reconstructed walls and computed measurements. Moving the lower endpoint changes the floor corner and reconstructed wall height; moving the upper endpoint preserves the footprint but changes height. Orange highlights affected geometry and changed measurements.

Structural consensus from 6 synthetic annotations. (a) Local walls locate the corresponding upper--lower pairs at K, with both endpoints used for matching; colors and symbols identify its 3 supporters. (b) Column layouts and row thumbnails identify who drew each corner. W has 6 supporters, K has exactly half and is retained, and E has only 2 and is omitted. A dot means the corner was not drawn. (c) K's upper elevation, unwrapped azimuth and lower elevation are sorted separately; orange boxes select each middle observation. Spacing shows rank, not angular distance. The upper and lower medians form a new pair with a shared median azimuth. (d) This pair becomes K in the complete layout, preserving its local wall height.

Q detects balanced local height distortion and preserves unchanged geometry under resampling. In the analytical 3 m reference room, (a) opposing height shifts preserve mean height and corner-mean prism IoU but reduce Q; (b) additional collinear pairs change corner-mean prism IoU while perimeter-based measurements and Q stay fixed.

Different members change support for the same recess in jtcxE69GiFV-13. Each team contains 10 people and requires 5 supporters per retained turn. Team 1 has 4 and 2 supporters for A and B; Team 2 has 8 for each. The resulting layouts contain 4 and 6 corners, respectively. Complete footprints use identical limits and equal axis scales across teams; the dotted boxes identify the region shown at right, also at identical limits and equal scales. Crosses mark below-threshold aggregate positions, not retained corners. Gray lines show individual walls and dashed lines show the reference. Coordinates are normalized by camera height $h$.

Structural response, relative quality and original drawings. (a--b) Annotator-level structural responses and quality ranks across difficulty conditions, using 58 and 59 people respectively; each dot represents 1 person. Relative Q is centered on the image--target peer median; higher within-image ranks indicate better relative quality. (c) The difficult panorama. (d--f) Submissions from C1--C3 on the panorama in (c) retain 5, 6 and 8 turns on a common BEV scale; gray dashes mark the reference and thick segments mark short walls.

Group size affects mean Q, lower-tail Q, between-team variation and output completion differently. Curves use the same 171 images: 116 easy, 28 moderate and 27 difficult. Q summaries use scorable outputs; complete-and-evaluable rates use all 43,776 attempts per size. P10 is the image-specific 10th percentile, averaged over images. Shading marks 3--6 and 20--30 people. The at-least-half threshold admits exactly half of an even-sized team: the required support stays at 2 votes from 3 to 4 people, then rises to 3 at 5 people, contributing to odd--even alternation.

Composition and member replacement. (a) 12-person teams on zsNo4HB9uLZ-16 retain 6 members and choose 6 of 12 candidates. Points show mean Q, bars the 5th--95th percentiles, and $n$ the scorable teams. (b--c) 14-person teams retain 7 members and exchange 7-person blocks in the A--B--C design. Each dot is an image mean; diamonds average 69 images from 146 scorable events. $G_S$ compares the average cross-class change magnitude with the within-class change magnitude; $Q_C-Q_B$ measures the signed quality change from B to C (Supplements C17, C19).

Whole-profile mixtures gain relative to one constituent and lose relative to another. Dots are paired image-level mixture-minus-pure Q differences on 154 common images; diamonds are means. Each selected profile contributes all its available \mbox{members}.

7 replacements change localization while 4 identities retain 20 votes and the same ring order in 7y3sRwLe3Va-13. Panels show the complete footprints, corner-4 detail and its upper/lower observations. Gray marks 13 retained people, blue 7 removed and orange 7 added; outlined markers are consensus positions. Changes of about 0.42 horizontal and 0.82 lower-endpoint pixels correspond to a floor displacement of $0.17h$ in the 1024 by 512 panorama. Q measures the complete layout.

2 annotators repeat their broader structural habits across views while changing individual corner choices. (a--b) A40 and A41's complete layouts on VFuaQ6m2Qom-07 and -10, with the same narrow-wall endpoints enlarged. Counts are effective/reference turns; dashed lines mark reference azimuths. A40 marks both endpoints in both views. A41 marks neither in view 07 and both in view 10, while simplifying both layouts. (c) Same-person and different-person simplification agreement over 15 view pairs in 5 buildings.

Enclosure choices at a doorway-boundary viewpoint. (a--b) The complete 3D model and panorama show the bathroom--hallway doorway. (c--e) Floor outlines from the same model illustrate the bathroom, hallway and combined enclosure at a common orientation and scale. Black dashed segments mark closure at either end of the threshold; white-backed circles locate the camera. The gray dotted outline provides the combined-space context.

Doorway outcomes. (a--b) Screening uses the same 17 images and whole-space reference before and after, at sizes 3--14. (c--d) Target-assigned pools for 7y3sRwLe3Va-18 contain 9 people for space 1, 4 for space 2 and 15 for the whole space; members and references differ. Q uses scorable outputs; completion is the complete-and-evaluable rate over all attempts.
